variable {E H M : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H) [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M]

/-- The cotangent bundle of a smooth manifold, constructed as the smooth vector bundle dual to its
 tangent bundle. -/
abbrev CotangentBundle :=
  TotalSpace (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) (fun x : M ↦ TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] ℝ)

/-- The model with corners on the total space of the cotangent bundle. -/
abbrev cotangentModel :
    ModelWithCorners ℝ (E × (E →L[ℝ] ℝ)) (ModelProd H (E →L[ℝ] ℝ)) :=
  I.prod 𝓘(ℝ, E →L[ℝ] ℝ)

variable [IsManifold I ∞ M] [CompleteSpace E]

/-- A (not necessarily smooth) real one-form on a manifold. -/
abbrev OneForm {F K N : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    [TopologicalSpace K] (J : ModelWithCorners ℝ F K) [TopologicalSpace N]
    [ChartedSpace K N] :=
  (x : N) → TangentSpace J x →L[ℝ] ℝ

/-- The manifold derivative of a real-valued function, viewed in the model space `ℝ`. -/
def scalarMFDeriv {F K N : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    [TopologicalSpace K] (J : ModelWithCorners ℝ F K) [TopologicalSpace N]
    [ChartedSpace K N] (f : N → ℝ) (x : N) : TangentSpace J x →L[ℝ] ℝ :=
  mfderiv J 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) f x

/-- The standard vector-field formula for the value of the exterior derivative of a one-form.
The existential clause ensures that the requested tangent vectors admit locally smooth vector-field
extensions; the universal clause makes the value independent of the chosen extensions. -/
def IsExteriorDerivativeAt {F K N : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    [TopologicalSpace K] (J : ModelWithCorners ℝ F K) [TopologicalSpace N]
    [ChartedSpace K N] [IsManifold J ∞ N] [CompleteSpace F]
    (α : OneForm (N := N) J) (x : N) (v w : TangentSpace J x) (r : ℝ) : Prop :=
  let smoothAt (V : (y : N) → TangentSpace J y) :=
    ContMDiffAt J (J.prod 𝓘(ℝ, F)) ∞
      (fun y ↦ (⟨y, V y⟩ : TangentBundle J N)) x
  let value (V W : (y : N) → TangentSpace J y) :=
    scalarMFDeriv J (fun y ↦ α y (W y)) x (V x) -
      scalarMFDeriv J (fun y ↦ α y (V y)) x (W x) -
        α x (VectorField.mlieBracket J V W x)
  (∃ V W, V x = v ∧ W x = w ∧ smoothAt V ∧ smoothAt W) ∧
    ∀ V W, V x = v → W x = w → smoothAt V → smoothAt W → value V W = r

/-- Pullback of a one-form by a differentiable map. -/
def pullbackOneForm {F K N : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    [TopologicalSpace K] (J : ModelWithCorners ℝ F K) [TopologicalSpace N]
    [ChartedSpace K N] {F' K' N' : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F'] [NormedSpace ℝ F']
    [TopologicalSpace K'] (J' : ModelWithCorners ℝ F' K') [TopologicalSpace N']
    [ChartedSpace K' N'] (f : N → N') (α : OneForm (N := N') J') : OneForm (N := N) J :=
  fun x ↦ α (f x) ∘L mfderiv J J' f x

/-- A one-form is exact if it is the differential of a smooth real-valued function. -/
def IsExactOneForm {F K N : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    [TopologicalSpace K] (J : ModelWithCorners ℝ F K) [TopologicalSpace N]
    [ChartedSpace K N] (α : OneForm (N := N) J) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : N → ℝ, ContMDiff J 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ∞ f ∧
    ∀ x, α x = mfderiv J 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) f x

/-- The canonical Liouville one-form on a cotangent bundle. At a covector `p`, it applies `p` to
the projection to the tangent space of the base. -/
def liouvilleForm : OneForm (N := CotangentBundle (M := M) I) (cotangentModel I) :=
  fun p ↦ p.2 ∘L mfderiv (cotangentModel I) I (π (E →L[ℝ] ℝ)
    (fun x : M ↦ TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] ℝ)) p

/-- A smooth embedding is an exact Lagrangian embedding in the cotangent bundle if it has the
right dimension, its pullback of the Liouville form is exact, and the exterior derivative of that
pullback vanishes. -/
def IsExactLagrangianEmbedding {F L : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    [CompleteSpace F] [TopologicalSpace L] [ChartedSpace F L] [IsManifold 𝓘(ℝ, F) ∞ L]
    (ι : L → CotangentBundle (M := M) I) : Prop :=
  Manifold.IsSmoothEmbedding 𝓘(ℝ, F) (cotangentModel I) ∞ ι ∧
    Module.finrank ℝ F = Module.finrank ℝ E ∧
    IsExactOneForm 𝓘(ℝ, F) (pullbackOneForm 𝓘(ℝ, F) (cotangentModel I) ι (liouvilleForm I)) ∧
    ∀ x v w, IsExteriorDerivativeAt 𝓘(ℝ, F)
      (pullbackOneForm 𝓘(ℝ, F) (cotangentModel I) ι (liouvilleForm I)) x v w 0

/-- A compactly supported Hamiltonian isotopy carries the zero section to an embedded submanifold
if it is generated on time `[0,1]` by a smooth, spatially compactly supported Hamiltonian through
the canonical symplectic form `dλ`. -/
def IsHamiltonianIsotopicToZeroSection {F L : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F]
    [NormedSpace ℝ F] [TopologicalSpace L] [ChartedSpace F L]
    (ι : L → CotangentBundle (M := M) I) : Prop :=
  let T := CotangentBundle (M := M) I
  let J := cotangentModel I
  ∃ (Hamil : ℝ → T → ℝ) (X : ℝ → (p : T) → TangentSpace J p)
      (Φ Ψ : ℝ → T → T),
    ContMDiff (𝓘(ℝ, ℝ).prod J) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ∞ (Function.uncurry Hamil) ∧
    IsCompact (closure {p | ∃ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, Hamil t p ≠ 0}) ∧
    (∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      ContMDiff J (J.prod 𝓘(ℝ, E × (E →L[ℝ] ℝ))) ∞
        (fun p ↦ (⟨p, X t p⟩ : TangentBundle J T))) ∧
    (∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ p v,
      IsExteriorDerivativeAt J (liouvilleForm I) p (X t p) v
        (-(scalarMFDeriv J (Hamil t) p v))) ∧
    ContMDiff (𝓘(ℝ, ℝ).prod J) J ∞ (Function.uncurry Φ) ∧
    (∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ContMDiff J J ∞ (Φ t) ∧ ContMDiff J J ∞ (Ψ t) ∧
      Function.LeftInverse (Ψ t) (Φ t) ∧ Function.RightInverse (Ψ t) (Φ t)) ∧
    (∀ p, Φ 0 p = p) ∧
    (∀ p t, t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 →
      HasMFDerivWithinAt 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) J (fun s ↦ Φ s p) (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) t
        ((1 : ℝ →L[ℝ] ℝ).smulRight (X t (Φ t p)))) ∧
    range (Φ 1 ∘ zeroSection (E →L[ℝ] ℝ)
      (fun x : M ↦ TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] ℝ)) = range ι

/-- **Nearby Lagrangian conjecture.** For every closed smooth manifold $M$, every closed exact
Lagrangian submanifold of $T^*M$ is the image of the zero section under the time-one map of a
compactly supported Hamiltonian flow. Here closed manifolds and submanifolds are taken to be
nonempty, compact, connected, and without boundary. -/
@[category research open, AMS 53 57]
theorem nearby_lagrangian_conjecture :
    ∀ (E : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
      (M : Type) [TopologicalSpace M] [T2Space M] [ChartedSpace E M]
      [IsManifold 𝓘(ℝ, E) ∞ M] [BoundarylessManifold 𝓘(ℝ, E) M]
      [CompactSpace M] [ConnectedSpace M] [Nonempty M]
      (F : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [FiniteDimensional ℝ F]
      (L : Type) [TopologicalSpace L] [T2Space L] [ChartedSpace F L]
      [IsManifold 𝓘(ℝ, F) ∞ L] [BoundarylessManifold 𝓘(ℝ, F) L]
      [CompactSpace L] [ConnectedSpace L] [Nonempty L]
      (ι : L → CotangentBundle (M := M) 𝓘(ℝ, E)),
      IsExactLagrangianEmbedding (M := M) (F := F) (L := L) 𝓘(ℝ, E) ι →
        IsHamiltonianIsotopicToZeroSection (M := M) (F := F) (L := L) 𝓘(ℝ, E) ι := by
  sorry

end

end NearbyLagrangianConjecture

Represented a Lagrangian submanifold by a smooth embedding `ι : L → T*M`; equality of ranges makes the claim independent of the chosen parametrization.
Constructed `T*M` as the smooth continuous-linear dual of Mathlib’s tangent bundle and defined the Liouville form by `λ_p(v) = p(dπ(v))`.

Defined the canonical symplectic form implicitly as `dλ`, using the standard vector-field/Lie-bracket formula for exterior derivatives. Lagrangian means the pullback of `dλ` vanishes and the embedded manifold has dimension equal to that of the base.
Defined exactness as existence of a smooth real potential whose manifold derivative equals the pullback of the Liouville form.

Interpreted compactly supported Hamiltonian isotopy as generated on `[0,1]` by a smooth time-dependent Hamiltonian whose spatial supports have compact total union (expressed by compactness of the closure), with a smooth flow satisfying the Hamiltonian ODE and consisting of diffeomorphisms.
Used the sign convention `ι_X(dλ) = -dH`; changing the sign of the Hamiltonian gives the opposite common convention without changing the resulting notion of Hamiltonian isotopy.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Nearby Lagrangian conjecture

The *nearby Lagrangian conjecture*, often attributed to Vladimir Arnold, states that any closed
exact Lagrangian submanifold of the cotangent bundle $T^*M$ of a closed manifold $M$ is
Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section.

Here $T^*M$ carries its canonical symplectic form $\omega = d\lambda$, where $\lambda$ is the
Liouville (or tautological) $1$-form, $\lambda_{(x, \xi)}(v) = \xi(d\pi_{(x, \xi)}(v))$ for
$\pi : T^*M \to M$ the bundle projection. A Lagrangian submanifold $L \subseteq T^*M$ is *exact*
if the restriction $\lambda|_L$ is an exact $1$-form.

Mathlib has neither differential forms on manifolds nor symplectic structures, so this file
introduces the required notions directly in terms of the Liouville form and `mfderiv`:

- `NearbyLagrangianConjecture.CotangentBundle E M` is the cotangent bundle $T^*M$, realised as the
  total space of the bundle of continuous linear functionals on the tangent spaces of `M`.
- `NearbyLagrangianConjecture.liouvilleForm` is the Liouville $1$-form $\lambda$ on $T^*M$.
- `NearbyLagrangianConjecture.IsExactLagrangianEmbedding ι` says that a smooth embedding
  `ι : L → T*M` of a manifold `L` of the same dimension as `M` satisfies
  $\iota^*\lambda = df$ for some smooth `f : L → ℝ`. Since $\omega = d\lambda$, this gives
  $\iota^*\omega = d(df) = 0$, so the image of `ι` is a Lagrangian submanifold, and it is exact
  by definition.
- `NearbyLagrangianConjecture.IsHamiltonianIsotopy φ` says that the compactly supported smooth
  family of diffeomorphisms `φ t` of $T^*M$ (with `φ 0 = id`) is a Hamiltonian isotopy. We use
  the standard characterisation on the exact symplectic manifold $(T^*M, \lambda)$: an isotopy
  $\varphi_t$ with $\varphi_0 = \mathrm{id}$ is Hamiltonian if and only if
  $\varphi_t^*\lambda - \lambda = dF_t$ for a smooth family of functions $F_t$. Indeed, if
  $X_t$ generates $\varphi_t$ then $\frac{d}{dt}\varphi_t^*\lambda =
  \varphi_t^*(\iota_{X_t}\omega + d(\lambda(X_t)))$, so $\iota_{X_t}\omega$ is exact for all $t$
  if and only if $\varphi_t^*\lambda - \lambda$ is exact for all $t$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Nearby Lagrangian conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nearby_Lagrangian_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
-/

open scoped Manifold ContDiff Bundle
open Bundle Function

namespace NearbyLagrangianConjecture

section Definitions

/-- The cotangent bundle $T^*M$ of a manifold `M` modelled on the normed space `E`: the total
space of the bundle whose fibre over `x : M` is the space of continuous linear functionals on the
tangent space of `M` at `x`. -/
abbrev CotangentBundle (E : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    (M : Type*) [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace E M] :=
  TotalSpace (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) (fun x : M => TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, E) x →L[ℝ] ℝ)

/-- The model with corners of the cotangent bundle of a boundaryless manifold modelled on `E`. -/
abbrev cotangentModel (E : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] :
    ModelWithCorners ℝ (E × (E →L[ℝ] ℝ)) (ModelProd E (E →L[ℝ] ℝ)) :=
  𝓘(ℝ, E).prod 𝓘(ℝ, E →L[ℝ] ℝ)

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  {M : Type*} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace E M] [IsManifold 𝓘(ℝ, E) ∞ M]

/-- The Liouville (tautological) $1$-form $\lambda$ on the cotangent bundle $T^*M$: at a point
$p = (x, \xi) \in T^*M$ and for a tangent vector $v \in T_p(T^*M)$, it is given by
$\lambda_p(v) = \xi(d\pi_p(v))$, where $\pi : T^*M \to M$ is the bundle projection. -/
noncomputable def liouvilleForm (p : CotangentBundle E M) :
    TangentSpace (cotangentModel E) p →L[ℝ] ℝ :=
  p.2.comp (mfderiv (cotangentModel E) 𝓘(ℝ, E) TotalSpace.proj p)

/-- The Liouville form vanishes along the zero section of $T^*M$. -/
@[category API, AMS 53 57]
theorem liouvilleForm_zeroSection (x : M) :
    liouvilleForm ((zeroSection _ _ : M → CotangentBundle E M) x) = 0 :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.zero_comp _

variable {L : Type*} [TopologicalSpace L] [ChartedSpace E L]

/-- A map `ι : L → T*M` from a manifold `L` modelled on the same normed space `E` as `M` (so that
$\dim L = \dim M$) is an *exact Lagrangian embedding* if it is a smooth embedding and the pull-back
$\iota^*\lambda$ of the Liouville form is exact, i.e. $\iota^*\lambda = df$ for some smooth
function $f : L \to \mathbb{R}$.

Since the canonical symplectic form is $\omega = d\lambda$, exactness of $\iota^*\lambda$ implies
$\iota^*\omega = d(\iota^*\lambda) = d(df) = 0$, so the image of `ι` is a Lagrangian submanifold of
$T^*M$; it is exact precisely when $\iota^*\lambda$ is exact. -/
structure IsExactLagrangianEmbedding (ι : L → CotangentBundle E M) : Prop where
  /-- `ι` is a smooth embedding. -/
  isSmoothEmbedding : Manifold.IsSmoothEmbedding 𝓘(ℝ, E) (cotangentModel E) ∞ ι
  /-- The pull-back $\iota^*\lambda$ of the Liouville form is exact: $\iota^*\lambda = df$ for a
  smooth function `f : L → ℝ`. -/
  exact : ∃ f : L → ℝ, ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ f ∧ ∀ x : L,
    (liouvilleForm (ι x)).comp (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) (cotangentModel E) ι x) =
      mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) f x

/-- A family `φ : ℝ → T*M ≃ₘ T*M` of diffeomorphisms of the cotangent bundle is a
(compactly supported) *Hamiltonian isotopy* if it depends smoothly on the parameter, starts at
the identity, is supported in a compact set, and $\varphi_t^*\lambda - \lambda = dF_t$ for a
smooth family of functions $F_t : T^*M \to \mathbb{R}$. The time parameter ranges over all of
$\mathbb{R}$ rather than $[0, 1]$; the two conventions are equivalent after reparametrising time.

The last condition is the standard characterisation of Hamiltonian isotopies of the exact
symplectic manifold $(T^*M, d\lambda)$: if $X_t$ is the time-dependent vector field generating
$\varphi_t$, then $\frac{d}{dt}\varphi_t^*\lambda = \varphi_t^*(\iota_{X_t}\omega +
d(\lambda(X_t)))$, so $\iota_{X_t}\omega$ is exact for every $t$ (i.e. $X_t$ is a Hamiltonian
vector field) if and only if $\varphi_t^*\lambda - \lambda$ is exact for every $t$. -/
structure IsHamiltonianIsotopy
    (φ : ℝ →
      CotangentBundle E M ≃ₘ⟮cotangentModel E, cotangentModel E⟯ CotangentBundle E M) :
    Prop where
  /-- The isotopy depends smoothly on the time parameter. -/
  contMDiff : ContMDiff (𝓘(ℝ).prod (cotangentModel E)) (cotangentModel E) ∞
    (fun q : ℝ × CotangentBundle E M => φ q.1 q.2)
  /-- The isotopy starts at the identity. -/
  apply_zero : ∀ p, φ 0 p = p
  /-- The isotopy is supported in a compact set. -/
  exists_isCompact : ∃ K : Set (CotangentBundle E M), IsCompact K ∧
    ∀ t, ∀ p ∉ K, φ t p = p
  /-- $\varphi_t^*\lambda - \lambda = dF_t$ for a smooth family of functions $F_t$. -/
  exists_primitive : ∃ F : ℝ → CotangentBundle E M → ℝ,
    ContMDiff (𝓘(ℝ).prod (cotangentModel E)) 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ (uncurry F) ∧ ∀ t p,
      (liouvilleForm (φ t p)).comp (mfderiv (cotangentModel E) (cotangentModel E) (φ t) p) -
        liouvilleForm p = mfderiv (cotangentModel E) 𝓘(ℝ) (F t) p

/-- The constant family at the identity is a Hamiltonian isotopy. -/
@[category test, AMS 53 57]
theorem isHamiltonianIsotopy_refl :
    IsHamiltonianIsotopy
      (fun _ : ℝ => Diffeomorph.refl (cotangentModel E) (CotangentBundle E M) ∞) where
  contMDiff := by simpa using contMDiff_snd
  apply_zero _ := rfl
  exists_isCompact := ⟨∅, isCompact_empty, fun _ _ _ => rfl⟩
  exists_primitive := ⟨fun _ _ => 0, contMDiff_const, fun _ _ => by simp [mfderiv_id]⟩

/-- The zero section of $T^*M$ is an exact Lagrangian embedding (with $f = 0$). -/
@[category test, AMS 53 57]
theorem isExactLagrangianEmbedding_zeroSection :
    IsExactLagrangianEmbedding
      (zeroSection _ _ : M → CotangentBundle E M) where
  isSmoothEmbedding := by
    refine ⟨⟨E →L[ℝ] ℝ, inferInstance, inferInstance, fun x => ?_⟩, ?_⟩
    · refine Manifold.IsImmersionAtOfComplement.mk_of_continuousAt
        (contMDiff_zeroSection ℝ _ (n := ∞) (IB := 𝓘(ℝ, E))).continuous.continuousAt
        (ContinuousLinearEquiv.refl ℝ _) (chartAt E x)
        (chartAt (ModelProd E (E →L[ℝ] ℝ)) (zeroSection _ _ x)) (mem_chart_source _ _)
        (mem_chart_source _ _) (IsManifold.chart_mem_maximalAtlas _)
        (IsManifold.chart_mem_maximalAtlas _) ?_

The single-slot decomposition is appropriate; the notes' reading (compact, boundaryless, connected M; exactness of λ|_L; Hamiltonian isotopy via compactly supported Hamiltonian flow) was followed, with the equivalent exact-symplectic characterisation used for the isotopy because ω = dλ cannot be written in Mathlib.
modeling_decisions: 'Closed manifold' is read as compact, Hausdorff, boundaryless (model with corners `𝓘(ℝ, E)` with `E` a finite-dimensional real normed space), smooth (`IsManifold 𝓘(ℝ, E) ∞`) and connected (`ConnectedSpace`), for both M and L. Connectedness of M is essential (otherwise the zero section over one component is a trivial counterexample); connectedness of L follows the usual convention and excludes the empty submanifold (for which the statement would be trivially false). It is known that closed exact Lagrangians in T*M (M connected) are connected, so this does not change the content.
The general finite-dimensional model space `E` is used instead of `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)`; this is equivalent.

The cotangent bundle T*M is `Bundle.TotalSpace (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) (fun x => TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, E) x →L[ℝ] ℝ)`, with model with corners `𝓘(ℝ, E).prod 𝓘(ℝ, E →L[ℝ] ℝ)`; Mathlib provides the smooth-manifold structure (`Bundle.TotalSpace.isManifold` via `ContMDiffVectorBundle.continuousLinearMap`).

A closed exact Lagrangian submanifold is encoded as the image of a smooth embedding `ι : L → T*M` (`Manifold.IsSmoothEmbedding`) of a closed manifold `L` charted on the same model `E` as `M` (so dim L = dim M automatically), rather than as a subset with a submanifold predicate (Mathlib has none). Every embedded closed submanifold arises this way.

Because Mathlib has no exterior derivative on manifolds, the symplectic form ω = dλ is never written. 'Exact Lagrangian' is encoded as: ι^*λ = df for a smooth f : L → ℝ (with λ the Liouville form λ_p = p.2 ∘ dπ_p). Since ω = dλ, exactness of ι^*λ implies ι^*ω = d(df) = 0, so together with dim L = dim M this is exactly 'Lagrangian and exact'; the Lagrangian condition is therefore not stated separately. Sign conventions for λ, ω play no role.

'Hamiltonian isotopy' is encoded (structure `IsHamiltonianIsotopy`) as a family φ : ℝ → Diffeomorph of T*M, jointly smooth in (t, p), with φ 0 = id, supported in a compact set (φ t p = p outside a compact K), and satisfying the exact-symplectic characterisation φ_t^*λ − λ = dF_t for a jointly smooth F : ℝ × T*M → ℝ. On the exact symplectic manifold (T*M, dλ) this is equivalent to φ_t being generated by Hamiltonian vector fields (d/dt φ_t^*λ = φ_t^*(ι_{X_t}ω + d λ(X_t))), avoiding both ω and ODE flows. Using compactly supported isotopies (rather than compactly supported Hamiltonian functions) and time parameter ℝ instead of [0,1] does not change which closed Lagrangians are Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section (cut-off and reparametrisation arguments).
'Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section' is `φ 1 '' Set.range (zeroSection …) = Set.range ι` for some Hamiltonian isotopy φ.

Two `@[category test]` sanity statements are proved (not sorried): the constant identity family is a Hamiltonian isotopy, and the zero section is an exact Lagrangian embedding; plus an `@[category API]` lemma that λ vanishes on the zero section. These confirm the hypotheses are satisfiable and the isotopy notion is non-vacuous.

The nearby Lagrangian conjecture asserts that every closed exact Lagrangian submanifold of the
cotangent bundle of a closed manifold is Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section.

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nearby_Lagrangian_conjecture)

/-- The pointwise data of a one-form on a manifold, as a continuous linear functional. -/
abbrev OneForm {E H M : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H) [TopologicalSpace M]
    [ChartedSpace H M] := ∀ x : M, TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] ℝ

/-- The pointwise data of a two-form on a manifold, as a continuous bilinear form. -/
abbrev TwoForm {E H M : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H) [TopologicalSpace M]
    [ChartedSpace H M] := ∀ x : M, TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] ℝ


/-- The differential of a real-valued function on a manifold. -/
def differential {E H M : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H) [TopologicalSpace M]
    [ChartedSpace H M] [IsManifold I 1 M] (f : M → ℝ) (x : M) : E →L[ℝ] ℝ :=
  fderivWithin ℝ (writtenInExtChartAt I 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) x f) (Set.range I) (extChartAt I x x)

/-- Data characterizing the canonical symplectic cotangent bundle of `M`.

Each fiber of `projection` is identified bijectively with the continuous dual of the tangent
space.  The Liouville form is evaluation of that covector on the derivative of the projection,
and `symplectic` is its exterior derivative, expressed by Cartan's formula. -/

    {E H M F K X : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [TopologicalSpace H]
    (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H) [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [TopologicalSpace K]
    (J : ModelWithCorners ℝ F K) [TopologicalSpace X] [ChartedSpace K X]
    [IsManifold J ∞ X] where
  projection : X → M
  projection_smooth : ContMDiff J I ∞ projection
  projection_submersion : ∀ x : X, Surjective (mfderiv J I projection x)
  covector : ∀ x : X, TangentSpace I (projection x) →L[ℝ] ℝ
  fiber_bijective : ∀ (m : M) (ξ : TangentSpace I m →L[ℝ] ℝ),
    ∃! x : X, ∃ h : projection x = m, h ▸ covector x = ξ
  liouville : OneForm (M := X) J
  liouville_smooth : ∀ (V : ∀ x : X, TangentSpace J x),
    ContMDiff J J.tangent ∞ (fun x ↦ (V x : TangentBundle J X)) →
    ContMDiff J 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ∞ (fun x ↦ liouville x (V x))
  liouville_eq : ∀ (x : X) (v : TangentSpace J x),
    liouville x v = covector x (mfderiv J I projection x v)
  symplectic : TwoForm (M := X) J
  symplectic_smooth : ∀ (U V : ∀ x : X, TangentSpace J x),
    ContMDiff J J.tangent ∞ (fun x ↦ (U x : TangentBundle J X)) →
    ContMDiff J J.tangent ∞ (fun x ↦ (V x : TangentBundle J X)) →
    ContMDiff J 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ∞ (fun x ↦ symplectic x (U x) (V x))
  symplectic_skew : ∀ (x : X) (u v : TangentSpace J x),

    (J : ModelWithCorners ℝ F K) [TopologicalSpace X] [ChartedSpace K X] [IsManifold J 1 X]
    [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace ℝ G] [TopologicalSpace Q]
    (L : ModelWithCorners ℝ G Q) [TopologicalSpace N] [ChartedSpace Q N] [IsManifold L 1 N]

import FormalConjecturesUtil
import Mathlib.Geometry.Manifold.SmoothEmbedding

/-!
# Nearby Lagrangian conjecture

The nearby Lagrangian conjecture concerns closed exact Lagrangian submanifolds of the
cotangent bundle of a closed manifold.

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nearby_Lagrangian_conjecture)
-/

open scoped Manifold Topology
open Bundle Set

namespace NearbyLagrangianConjecture

/-- The cotangent space at `x`, defined as the continuous dual of the tangent space. -/
abbrev CotangentSpace {E M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E E) [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace E M] (x : M) :=
  TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] ℝ

/-- The cotangent bundle, as the total space of the continuous dual of the tangent bundle. -/
abbrev CotangentBundle {E M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E E) [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace E M] :=
  Bundle.TotalSpace (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) (CotangentSpace (M := M) I)

/-- The manifold model of a cotangent bundle. -/
abbrev cotangentBundleModel {E : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E E) :=
  I.prod 𝓘(ℝ, E →L[ℝ] ℝ)

/-- The canonical Liouville one-form on a cotangent bundle. At a covector `p`, it applies `p`
to the projection of a tangent vector to the base. -/
noncomputable def liouvilleForm {E M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E E) [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace E M] [IsManifold I ⊤ M]
    (p : CotangentBundle I (M := M)) :
    TangentSpace (cotangentBundleModel I) p →L[ℝ] ℝ :=
  p.2.comp (mfderiv (cotangentBundleModel I) I
    (Bundle.TotalSpace.proj : CotangentBundle I (M := M) → M) p)

/-- A smooth embedding of an `E`-dimensional manifold into `T*M` is exact Lagrangian when the
pullback of the Liouville form is the differential of a smooth real-valued function. The shared
model space `E` gives the embedded manifold half the dimension of `T*M`; exactness then implies
the Lagrangian condition for the canonical symplectic form `dλ`. -/
def IsExactLagrangianEmbedding {E M N : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E E) [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace E M] [IsManifold I ⊤ M]
    [TopologicalSpace N] [ChartedSpace E N] (i : N → CotangentBundle I (M := M)) : Prop :=
  Manifold.IsSmoothEmbedding I (cotangentBundleModel I) ⊤ i ∧
    ∃ f : N → ℝ, ContMDiff I 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ⊤ f ∧
      ∀ (x : N) (v : TangentSpace I x),
        liouvilleForm I (i x) (mfderiv I (cotangentBundleModel I) i x v) =
          mfderiv I 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) f x v

/-- Two subsets of a cotangent bundle are Hamiltonian isotopic if one is carried to the other by
the time-one map of a compactly supported smooth exact symplectic isotopy starting at the identity.
For an exact symplectic manifold, this is the standard characterization of a compactly supported
Hamiltonian isotopy. -/
def AreHamiltonianIsotopic {E M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E E) [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace E M] [IsManifold I ⊤ M]
    (A B : Set (CotangentBundle I (M := M))) : Prop :=
  ∃ (Φ Ψ : ℝ → CotangentBundle I (M := M) → CotangentBundle I (M := M))
      (G : ℝ → CotangentBundle I (M := M) → ℝ) (K : Set (CotangentBundle I (M := M))),
    IsCompact K ∧
    ContMDiff (𝓘(ℝ, ℝ).prod (cotangentBundleModel I)) (cotangentBundleModel I) ⊤
      (fun z : ℝ × CotangentBundle I (M := M) ↦ Φ z.1 z.2) ∧
    ContMDiff (𝓘(ℝ, ℝ).prod (cotangentBundleModel I)) (cotangentBundleModel I) ⊤
      (fun z : ℝ × CotangentBundle I (M := M) ↦ Ψ z.1 z.2) ∧
    ContMDiff (𝓘(ℝ, ℝ).prod (cotangentBundleModel I)) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ⊤
      (fun z : ℝ × CotangentBundle I (M := M) ↦ G z.1 z.2) ∧
    (∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, Function.LeftInverse (Ψ t) (Φ t) ∧
      Function.RightInverse (Ψ t) (Φ t)) ∧
    Φ 0 = id ∧
    (∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, EqOn (Φ t) id Kᶜ) ∧
    (∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ (x : CotangentBundle I (M := M))
      (v : TangentSpace (cotangentBundleModel I) x),
      liouvilleForm I (Φ t x)
          (mfderiv (cotangentBundleModel I) (cotangentBundleModel I) (Φ t) x v) -
        liouvilleForm I x v =
          mfderiv (cotangentBundleModel I) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) (G t) x v) ∧
    Φ 1 '' A = B

/--
**Nearby Lagrangian conjecture.** Any closed exact Lagrangian submanifold of the cotangent
bundle of a closed connected smooth manifold is Hamiltonian isotopic, by a compactly supported
Hamiltonian isotopy, to the zero section.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 53 57]
theorem nearby_lagrangian_conjecture :
    ∀ (E M N : Type) (_ : NormedAddCommGroup E) (_ : NormedSpace ℝ E)
      (_ : FiniteDimensional ℝ E) (_ : TopologicalSpace M) (_ : ChartedSpace E M)
      (_ : IsManifold 𝓘(ℝ, E) ⊤ M) (_ : T2Space M) (_ : SecondCountableTopology M)
      (_ : CompactSpace M) (_ : ConnectedSpace M) (_ : TopologicalSpace N)
      (_ : ChartedSpace E N) (_ : IsManifold 𝓘(ℝ, E) ⊤ N) (_ : T2Space N)
      (_ : SecondCountableTopology N) (_ : CompactSpace N) (_ : ConnectedSpace N)
      (i : N → CotangentBundle 𝓘(ℝ, E) (M := M)),
      IsExactLagrangianEmbedding 𝓘(ℝ, E) i →
        AreHamiltonianIsotopic 𝓘(ℝ, E)
          (Set.range (Bundle.zeroSection (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) (CotangentSpace (M := M) 𝓘(ℝ, E))))
          (Set.range i) := by
  sorry

end NearbyLagrangianConjecture
modeling_decisions: A closed smooth manifold is modeled as a compact, connected, Hausdorff, second-countable finite-dimensional real smooth manifold without boundary. Boundarylessness is enforced by using Mathlib's boundaryless self model `𝓘(ℝ, E)`; both the base and the parametrizing manifold are modeled on the same finite-dimensional space `E`.

A closed Lagrangian submanifold is represented by a smooth embedding `i : N → T*M` from a compact connected manifold `N`. Using the same model space `E` for `M` and `N` enforces that `N` has half the dimension of `T*M`; compactness and the Hausdorff target make its image closed.

Exactness is stated directly as `i^*λ = df` for a smooth function `f`, where `λ` is the canonical Liouville form. Together with the half-dimension embedding, this implies the Lagrangian condition for the canonical symplectic form `dλ`, so no unavailable exterior-derivative API is postulated.

Hamiltonian isotopy is encoded by the standard equivalent characterization on an exact symplectic manifold: a smooth compactly supported isotopy through diffeomorphisms, starting at the identity, for which `Φ_t^*λ - λ = dG_t` with a jointly smooth family of potentials. A single compact set supports the isotopy for all `t ∈ [0,1]`.
The endpoint equation is oriented from the zero section to the given Lagrangian image. Hamiltonian isotopy is symmetric, so this faithfully expresses isotopy to the zero section.

All manifold and model types are placed in Lean universe `Type` to avoid dependent total-space universe ambiguity; this does not restrict the ordinary finite-dimensional manifolds intended by the conjecture.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Nearby Lagrangian conjecture

The nearby Lagrangian conjecture, usually attributed to Arnold, states that every closed exact
Lagrangian submanifold of the cotangent bundle $T^*M$ of a closed manifold $M$ is Hamiltonian
isotopic to the zero section.

Mathlib has no cotangent bundles with their symplectic structure, no exterior derivative on
manifolds and no Hamiltonian flows. This file builds the needed notions on top of Mathlib's
`C^∞` vector bundles:

* `CotangentBundle n M` is the total space of the bundle of continuous linear maps
  `TangentSpace (𝓡 n) q →L[ℝ] ℝ`; Mathlib makes it a smooth manifold.
* `liouvilleForm n M` is the Liouville (tautological) one-form $\lambda_{(q, p)} = p \circ d\pi$.
* `mextDerivOneForm I α` is the exterior derivative of a one-form on a manifold, computed in the
  extended chart at each point using Mathlib's `extDeriv`; `canonicalSymplecticForm n M` is
  $\omega = d\lambda$.
* `IsHamiltonianFlow n M H φ` says that `φ` is the flow of the Hamiltonian vector field of the
  time-dependent Hamiltonian `H`, and `IsHamiltonianIsotopic n M L₀ L₁` says that `L₁` is the
  image of `L₀` under the time-one map of such a flow.
* `IsExactLagrangianEmbedding ι` says that `ι : L → T^*M` is a smooth embedding of an
  $n$-manifold `L` with $\iota^*\omega = 0$ and $\iota^*\lambda$ exact.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Nearby Lagrangian conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nearby_Lagrangian_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [The nearby Lagrangian conjecture, Princeton Mathematics events](https://www.math.princeton.edu/events/nearby-lagrangian-conjecture-2020-03-05t173000)
-/

namespace NearbyLagrangianConjecture

open scoped Manifold ContDiff
open Bundle Manifold Set

section ExteriorDerivative

variable {E H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [TopologicalSpace H]
  (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H) {N : Type*} [TopologicalSpace N] [ChartedSpace H N]

/--
The exterior derivative of a one-form `α` on a manifold `N`, as a $2$-form.

At `x₀ : N`, write `α` in the extended chart `φ = extChartAt I x₀`: this gives the one-form
`y ↦ α (φ.symm y) ∘ D(φ.symm) y` on the model space `E`. Its exterior derivative (Mathlib's
`extDeriv`) at `φ x₀` is then pulled back along `D φ x₀ : TangentSpace I x₀ →L[ℝ] E`.
By naturality of the exterior derivative, this does not depend on the chart when `α` is
smooth and `x₀` is an interior point. This is the same pattern that Mathlib uses for
`VectorField.mlieBracket`.
-/
def mextDerivOneForm (α : Π x : N, TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] ℝ) (x₀ : N) :
    TangentSpace I x₀ [⋀^Fin 2]→L[ℝ] ℝ :=
  let φ := extChartAt I x₀
  let αφ : E → E [⋀^Fin 1]→L[ℝ] ℝ := fun y ↦
    ContinuousAlternatingMap.ofSubsingleton ℝ E ℝ 0
      ((α (φ.symm y)).comp (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) I φ.symm y))
  (extDeriv αφ (φ x₀)).compContinuousLinearMap (mfderiv I 𝓘(ℝ, E) φ x₀)

end ExteriorDerivative

section CotangentBundle

variable (n : ℕ) (M : Type*) [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) M]

/-- The cotangent space $T^*_qM = (T_qM)^*$ of an `n`-dimensional real manifold `M` at `q`,
realised as the fibre at `q` of the bundle of continuous linear maps from `TangentSpace (𝓡 n)`
to the trivial line bundle. -/
abbrev CotangentSpace (q : M) : Type _ :=
  TangentSpace (𝓡 n) q →L[ℝ] Bundle.Trivial M ℝ q

/-- The cotangent bundle $T^*M$ of an `n`-dimensional real manifold `M`, i.e. the total space of
the bundle of cotangent spaces. Mathlib provides its structure of `C^∞` vector bundle and of
`C^∞` manifold modelled on `cotangentModel n`. -/
abbrev CotangentBundle : Type _ :=
  TotalSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (CotangentSpace n M)

/-- The model with corners of the cotangent bundle of an `n`-dimensional real manifold: the
product of `𝓡 n` with the model on the fibre `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) →L[ℝ] ℝ`. -/
abbrev cotangentModel :
    ModelWithCorners ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) × (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) →L[ℝ] ℝ))
      (ModelProd (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) →L[ℝ] ℝ)) :=
  (𝓡 n).prod 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) →L[ℝ] ℝ)

/-- The zero section of $T^*M$, as a subset of `CotangentBundle n M`. -/
def zeroSectionSet : Set (CotangentBundle n M) :=
  range (zeroSection (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (CotangentSpace n M))

variable [IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ M]

/-- The Liouville (tautological) one-form $\lambda$ on $T^*M$: at the point $x = (q, p)$ with
$p \in T^*_qM$, it is $\lambda_x = p \circ d\pi_x$ where $\pi : T^*M \to M$ is the bundle
projection. -/
def liouvilleForm (x : CotangentBundle n M) : TangentSpace (cotangentModel n) x →L[ℝ] ℝ :=
  (x.2 : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x.proj →L[ℝ] ℝ).comp
    (mfderiv (cotangentModel n) (𝓡 n) TotalSpace.proj x)

/-- The canonical symplectic form $\omega = d\lambda$ on $T^*M$, where $\lambda$ is the Liouville
form. (Some authors use the opposite sign convention $\omega = -d\lambda$; this does not affect
the notions of Lagrangian submanifold or of Hamiltonian isotopy.) -/
def canonicalSymplecticForm (x : CotangentBundle n M) :
    TangentSpace (cotangentModel n) x [⋀^Fin 2]→L[ℝ] ℝ :=
  mextDerivOneForm (cotangentModel n) (liouvilleForm n M) x

/-- The Liouville form vanishes along the zero section of $T^*M$. -/
@[category API, AMS 53 57]
theorem liouvilleForm_zeroSection (q : M) :
    liouvilleForm n M
      (zeroSection (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (CotangentSpace n M) q) = 0 := by
  simp [liouvilleForm]

/--
`IsHamiltonianFlow n M H φ` means that `φ : ℝ → T^*M → T^*M` is the flow of the
(time-dependent) Hamiltonian `H : ℝ → T^*M → ℝ`. That is:
* `H` is smooth as a function of `(t, x)`;
* `φ 0 = id`;
* there is a time-dependent vector field `X` with $\omega(X_t, \cdot) = dH_t$ (the Hamiltonian
  vector field of `H`; it is unique since $\omega$ is nondegenerate) such that for every `x`,
  the curve `t ↦ φ t x` is an integral curve of `X`, i.e. `∂ₜ (φ t x) = X t (φ t x)`
  for all `t : ℝ`.
The flow is required to exist for all times and all starting points. The sign convention for
the Hamiltonian vector field is immaterial (replace `H` by `-H`).
-/
def IsHamiltonianFlow (H : ℝ → CotangentBundle n M → ℝ)
    (φ : ℝ → CotangentBundle n M → CotangentBundle n M) : Prop :=
  ContMDiff (𝓘(ℝ, ℝ).prod (cotangentModel n)) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ∞ (Function.uncurry H) ∧
  φ 0 = id ∧
  ∃ X : ℝ → Π x : CotangentBundle n M, TangentSpace (cotangentModel n) x,
    (∀ t x v, canonicalSymplecticForm n M x ![X t x, v] =
      mfderiv (cotangentModel n) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) (H t) x v) ∧
    ∀ x t, HasMFDerivAt 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) (cotangentModel n) (fun s ↦ φ s x) t
      ((1 : ℝ →L[ℝ] ℝ).smulRight (X t (φ t x)))

/-- Two subsets `L₀ L₁` of $T^*M$ are Hamiltonian isotopic if `L₁` is the image of `L₀` under
the time-one map of the flow of some time-dependent Hamiltonian on $T^*M$.

For compact `L₀`, cutting off the Hamiltonian near the (compact) trace of the isotopy shows that
this is equivalent to asking for a compactly supported Hamiltonian. -/
def IsHamiltonianIsotopic (L₀ L₁ : Set (CotangentBundle n M)) : Prop :=
  ∃ H φ, IsHamiltonianFlow n M H φ ∧ φ 1 '' L₀ = L₁

variable {n M} {L : Type*} [TopologicalSpace L] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) L]

/--
`IsExactLagrangianEmbedding ι` means that `ι : L → T^*M`, where `L` is an `n`-dimensional
manifold and `M` is an `n`-dimensional manifold, is an exact Lagrangian embedding:
* `ι` is a smooth embedding, so that `range ι` is an `n`-dimensional submanifold of the
  `2n`-dimensional manifold $T^*M$;
* `range ι` is isotropic, $\iota^*\omega = 0$, hence Lagrangian since it has half the dimension
  of $T^*M$;
* `range ι` is exact: the restriction $\iota^*\lambda$ of the Liouville form is exact, i.e.
  $\iota^*\lambda = df$ for some smooth `f : L → ℝ`.
-/
structure IsExactLagrangianEmbedding (ι : L → CotangentBundle n M) : Prop where
  isSmoothEmbedding : IsSmoothEmbedding (𝓡 n) (cotangentModel n) ∞ ι
  isotropic : ∀ (x : L) (v w : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x),
    canonicalSymplecticForm n M (ι x)
      ![mfderiv (𝓡 n) (cotangentModel n) ι x v, mfderiv (𝓡 n) (cotangentModel n) ι x w] = 0
  exact : ∃ f : L → ℝ, ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ∞ f ∧
    ∀ (x : L) (v : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x),
      liouvilleForm n M (ι x) (mfderiv (𝓡 n) (cotangentModel n) ι x v) =
        mfderiv (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) f x v

end CotangentBundle

/--
**Nearby Lagrangian conjecture.** "Any closed exact Lagrangian submanifold of the cotangent
bundle of a closed manifold is Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section."

Precisely: let $M$ be a closed (compact, boundaryless, connected) smooth manifold of dimension
$n$, and let $L \subseteq T^*M$ be a closed (compact, boundaryless, connected) exact Lagrangian
submanifold of its cotangent bundle, equipped with the canonical symplectic form
$\omega = d\lambda$. Then there is a (time-dependent) Hamiltonian on $T^*M$ whose time-one flow
maps the zero section onto $L$.

Here `M` and `L` are smooth manifolds modelled on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)` (so they have no
boundary), and the submanifold is given as the range of an exact Lagrangian embedding
`ι : L → T^*M`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 53 57]
theorem nearby_lagrangian_conjecture {n : ℕ} (M : Type*) [TopologicalSpace M] [T2Space M]
    [CompactSpace M] [ConnectedSpace M] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) M]
    [IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ M]
    (L : Type*) [TopologicalSpace L] [CompactSpace L] [ConnectedSpace L]
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) L] [IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ L]
    (ι : L → CotangentBundle n M) (hι : IsExactLagrangianEmbedding ι) :
    IsHamiltonianIsotopic n M (zeroSectionSet n M) (range ι) := by
  sorry

end NearbyLagrangianConjecture

end

The single-slot decomposition is appropriate; its notes (closed = compact, boundaryless, connected; exactness of λ|_L; Hamiltonian isotopy via time-one map of a Hamiltonian flow; nothing available in Mathlib) match what was formalized. The only nuance: the note's parenthetical '(compactly supported)' was implemented in the equivalent form 'flow defined for all times', as recorded in modeling decisions.
modeling_decisions: 'Closed manifold' M is taken as compact, Hausdorff, connected, boundaryless (model `𝓡 n` on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)`, so no boundary) C^∞ manifold. Connectedness of M is necessary for the statement to be non-trivially false; T2 is the usual manifold convention.

The closed exact Lagrangian submanifold is represented as the range of a smooth embedding ι : L → T*M from a compact, connected, boundaryless n-manifold L (dimension n = dim M is forced by L's model space, giving the half-dimension condition). Connectedness of L follows the usual convention (also in the decomposition notes); the statement without it is equivalent modulo the known theorem that closed exact Lagrangians in T*M pairwise intersect.

'Lagrangian' is stated literally as ι^*ω = 0 together with dim L = n; 'exact' as ι^*λ = df for a smooth f : L → ℝ. The isotropy condition is mathematically redundant given exactness (ι^*ω = d(ι^*λ) = ddf = 0) but is kept to match the phrase 'exact Lagrangian' literally.

The symplectic form is ω = dλ (sign convention immaterial for Lagrangian/Hamiltonian notions). The exterior derivative on the manifold T*M is computed in the extended chart at each point via Mathlib's `extDeriv`; this is chart-independent for smooth forms at interior points (T*M is boundaryless). The Hamiltonian vector field is characterised by ω(X_t,·) = dH_t (∃ X; unique since ω is nondegenerate, a fact not proven in the file). Sign convention immaterial (H ↦ -H).

'Hamiltonian isotopic' means: there is a jointly smooth time-dependent Hamiltonian H : ℝ × T*M → ℝ whose flow φ (φ 0 = id, every t ↦ φ t x an integral curve of X_t for all t ∈ ℝ and all x) satisfies φ 1 '' (zero section) = range ι. import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Nearby Lagrangian conjecture

The nearby Lagrangian conjecture, attributed to Vladimir Arnold, states that every closed exact
Lagrangian submanifold $L$ of the cotangent bundle $T^*M$ of a closed manifold $M$ (with its
canonical symplectic structure $\omega = d\lambda$, where $\lambda$ is the Liouville form) is
Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section.

Mathlib has no cotangent bundle, symplectic form or Hamiltonian flow, so this file sets up:

* the cotangent bundle $T^*M$ as the bundle of continuous linear maps from the tangent bundle
  to the trivial line bundle;
* the Liouville $1$-form $\lambda_{(x, p)}(v) = p(d\pi(v))$;
* the exterior derivative of a $1$-form on a manifold, computed in a chart, which gives the
  canonical symplectic form $\omega = d\lambda$;
* (compactly supported) Hamiltonian isotopies of $T^*M$, i.e. smooth families $\psi_t$ with
  $\psi_0 = \mathrm{id}$ and $\omega(\partial_t \psi_t(z), \cdot) = dH_t(\psi_t(z))$ for a smooth
  compactly supported time-dependent Hamiltonian $H$;
* closed exact Lagrangian submanifolds, given as smooth embeddings $\iota \colon L \to T^*M$ of a
  closed manifold $L$ of the same dimension as $M$ with $\iota^*\omega = 0$ and
  $\iota^*\lambda = df$ exact.

Conventions: manifolds are smooth ($C^\infty$), Hausdorff and finite-dimensional; a closed
manifold is compact, boundaryless and connected. Hamiltonian isotopies are generated by compactly
supported time-dependent Hamiltonians, as usual on the non-compact manifold $T^*M$; this does not
change the conjecture, since a Hamiltonian isotopy can be cut off outside a neighbourhood of the
compact set swept out by the zero section.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Nearby Lagrangian conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nearby_Lagrangian_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [AK18] Abouzaid, M., Kragh, T., *Simple homotopy equivalence of nearby Lagrangians*,
  Acta Math. 220 (2018), 207-237.
-/

namespace NearbyLagrangianConjecture

open scoped Manifold ContDiff

section Definitions

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  {H : Type*} [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H)
  (M : Type*) [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] [IsManifold I ∞ M]

/-- The cotangent space $T^*_xM = (T_xM)^*$ at a point `x` of a manifold `M`, as the fibre of
the bundle of continuous linear maps from the tangent bundle to the trivial line bundle. -/
abbrev CotangentSpace (x : M) : Type _ := TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] Bundle.Trivial M ℝ x

/-- The cotangent bundle $T^*M$ of a manifold `M`, i.e. the total space of `CotangentSpace I M`.
It is a smooth manifold modelled on `I.prod 𝓘(ℝ, E →L[ℝ] ℝ)`. -/
abbrev CotangentBundle : Type _ := Bundle.TotalSpace (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) (CotangentSpace I M)

/-- The zero section $0_M \subseteq T^*M$, as a set. -/
def zeroSection : Set (CotangentBundle I M) :=
  Set.range (Bundle.zeroSection (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) (CotangentSpace I M))

/-- The Liouville (canonical) $1$-form on $T^*M$: at $z = (x, p) \in T^*M$ it is
$\lambda_z(v) = p(d\pi_z(v))$, where $\pi \colon T^*M \to M$ is the bundle projection. -/
noncomputable def liouvilleForm (z : CotangentBundle I M) :
    TangentSpace (I.prod 𝓘(ℝ, E →L[ℝ] ℝ)) z →L[ℝ] ℝ :=
  (z.snd : TangentSpace I z.proj →L[ℝ] ℝ).comp
    (mfderiv (I.prod 𝓘(ℝ, E →L[ℝ] ℝ)) I (Bundle.TotalSpace.proj : CotangentBundle I M → M) z)

variable {E' : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E'] [NormedSpace ℝ E']
  {H' : Type*} [TopologicalSpace H'] (J : ModelWithCorners ℝ E' H')
  {N : Type*} [TopologicalSpace N] [ChartedSpace H' N]

/-- The exterior derivative $d\alpha$ of a $1$-form `α` on a manifold `N`, evaluated at `z` on
the tangent vectors `u`, `w`. It is computed in the chart $e = $ `extChartAt J z`: the coordinate
expression of `α` is the $1$-form $\tilde\alpha(y) = \alpha_{e^{-1}(y)} \circ d(e^{-1})_y$ on
the model space, whose exterior derivative (`extDerivWithin`, within the target of $e$) is
evaluated at $e(z)$ on the images of `u`, `w` under $de_z$. -/
noncomputable def extDerivOneForm (α : (z : N) → TangentSpace J z →L[ℝ] ℝ) (z : N)
    (u w : TangentSpace J z) : ℝ :=
  extDerivWithin
    (fun y : E' ↦ ContinuousAlternatingMap.ofSubsingleton ℝ E' ℝ (0 : Fin 1)
      ((α ((extChartAt J z).symm y)).comp (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E') J (extChartAt J z).symm y)))
    (extChartAt J z).target (extChartAt J z z)
    ![mfderiv J 𝓘(ℝ, E') (extChartAt J z) z u, mfderiv J 𝓘(ℝ, E') (extChartAt J z) z w]

/-- The canonical symplectic form $\omega = d\lambda$ on $T^*M$, evaluated at `z` on the tangent
vectors `u`, `w`. (Some authors use the opposite sign convention $\omega = -d\lambda$; this does
not affect the notions of Lagrangian submanifold or Hamiltonian isotopy.) -/
noncomputable def canonicalSymplecticForm (z : CotangentBundle I M)
    (u w : TangentSpace (I.prod 𝓘(ℝ, E →L[ℝ] ℝ)) z) : ℝ :=
  extDerivOneForm (I.prod 𝓘(ℝ, E →L[ℝ] ℝ)) (liouvilleForm I M) z u w

/-- A (compactly supported) Hamiltonian isotopy of $T^*M$: a smooth family
$\psi_t \colon T^*M \to T^*M$, $t \in \mathbb{R}$, with $\psi_0 = \mathrm{id}$, which is the flow
of the Hamiltonian vector field $X_{H_t}$ of a smooth time-dependent Hamiltonian
$H \colon \mathbb{R} \times T^*M \to \mathbb{R}$ supported in a fixed compact set, i.e.
$\omega(\partial_t \psi_t(z), v) = dH_t(\psi_t(z))(v)$ for all $t$, $z$ and $v$. -/
structure IsHamiltonianIsotopy (ψ : ℝ → CotangentBundle I M → CotangentBundle I M) : Prop where
  contMDiff : ContMDiff (𝓘(ℝ).prod (I.prod 𝓘(ℝ, E →L[ℝ] ℝ))) (I.prod 𝓘(ℝ, E →L[ℝ] ℝ)) ∞
    (Function.uncurry ψ)
  zero_eq_id : ψ 0 = id
  exists_hamiltonian : ∃ H : ℝ → CotangentBundle I M → ℝ,
    ContMDiff (𝓘(ℝ).prod (I.prod 𝓘(ℝ, E →L[ℝ] ℝ))) 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ (Function.uncurry H) ∧
    (∃ K : Set (CotangentBundle I M), IsCompact K ∧ ∀ t, ∀ z ∉ K, H t z = 0) ∧
    ∀ t z v, canonicalSymplecticForm I M (ψ t z)
      (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ) (I.prod 𝓘(ℝ, E →L[ℝ] ℝ)) (fun s ↦ ψ s z) t 1) v =
        mfderiv (I.prod 𝓘(ℝ, E →L[ℝ] ℝ)) 𝓘(ℝ) (H t) (ψ t z) v

/-- Two subsets `L`, `L'` of $T^*M$ are Hamiltonian isotopic if `L'` is the image of `L` under the
time-one map of a (compactly supported) Hamiltonian isotopy of $T^*M$. -/
def HamiltonianIsotopic (L L' : Set (CotangentBundle I M)) : Prop :=
  ∃ ψ, IsHamiltonianIsotopy I M ψ ∧ ψ 1 '' L = L'

/-- The Liouville form vanishes along the zero section. -/
@[category API, AMS 53 57]
lemma liouvilleForm_zeroSection (x : M) :
    liouvilleForm I M (Bundle.zeroSection (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) (CotangentSpace I M) x) = 0 :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.zero_comp _

/-- The canonical symplectic form vanishes when its first argument is zero. -/
@[category API, AMS 53 57]
lemma canonicalSymplecticForm_zero_left (z : CotangentBundle I M)
    (v : TangentSpace (I.prod 𝓘(ℝ, E →L[ℝ] ℝ)) z) :
    canonicalSymplecticForm I M z 0 v = 0 :=
  ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_coord_zero _ 0 (ContinuousLinearMap.map_zero _)

/-- The constant family `ψ t = id` is a Hamiltonian isotopy, generated by the zero Hamiltonian. -/
@[category API, AMS 53 57]
lemma isHamiltonianIsotopy_id : IsHamiltonianIsotopy I M (fun _ ↦ id) where
  contMDiff := contMDiff_snd
  zero_eq_id := rfl
  exists_hamiltonian :=
    ⟨fun _ _ ↦ 0, contMDiff_const, ⟨∅, isCompact_empty, fun _ _ _ ↦ rfl⟩, fun t z v ↦ by
      simp [mfderiv_const, canonicalSymplecticForm_zero_left]⟩

/-- Every subset of $T^*M$ is Hamiltonian isotopic to itself. -/
@[category API, AMS 53 57]
lemma hamiltonianIsotopic_refl (L : Set (CotangentBundle I M)) : HamiltonianIsotopic I M L L :=
  ⟨fun _ ↦ id, isHamiltonianIsotopy_id I M, Set.image_id L⟩

end Definitions

section Lagrangian

variable {n : ℕ} {M : Type*} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) M]
  [IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ M] {L : Type*} [TopologicalSpace L]
  [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) L]

/-- A map `ι : L → T*M` from an `n`-manifold `L` to the cotangent bundle of an `n`-manifold `M`
is an exact Lagrangian embedding if it is a smooth embedding whose image is Lagrangian
(isotropic, $\iota^*\omega = 0$, and of half dimension, $\dim L = \dim M = n$) and exact
($\iota^*\lambda = df$ for some smooth $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$). The isotropy condition is
implied by exactness, as $\iota^*\omega = d(\iota^*\lambda) = ddf = 0$; it is kept to match the
usual definition. -/
structure IsExactLagrangianEmbedding (ι : L → CotangentBundle (𝓡 n) M) : Prop where
  isSmoothEmbedding :
    Manifold.IsSmoothEmbedding (𝓡 n) ((𝓡 n).prod 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) →L[ℝ] ℝ)) ∞ ι
  isLagrangian : ∀ y u v, canonicalSymplecticForm (𝓡 n) M (ι y)
    (mfderiv (𝓡 n) ((𝓡 n).prod 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) →L[ℝ] ℝ)) ι y u)
    (mfderiv (𝓡 n) ((𝓡 n).prod 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) →L[ℝ] ℝ)) ι y v) = 0
  exact : ∃ f : L → ℝ, ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ f ∧ ∀ y v,
    liouvilleForm (𝓡 n) M (ι y)
      (mfderiv (𝓡 n) ((𝓡 n).prod 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) →L[ℝ] ℝ)) ι y v) =
        mfderiv (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ) f y v

end Lagrangian

/--
**Nearby Lagrangian conjecture.** Let $M$ be a closed (compact, boundaryless, connected) smooth
manifold of dimension $n$. Then every closed exact Lagrangian submanifold $L \subseteq T^*M$ is
Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section $0_M$. Here $L$ is the image of a smooth embedding
$\iota \colon L \to T^*M$ of a closed $n$-manifold with $\iota^*\omega = 0$ and $\iota^*\lambda$
exact, where $\lambda$ is the Liouville form and $\omega = d\lambda$ the canonical symplectic form.
The conclusion says $L = \psi_1(0_M)$ for the time-one map $\psi_1$ of a compactly supported
Hamiltonian isotopy $(\psi_t)$ of $T^*M$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 53 57]
theorem nearby_lagrangian_conjecture (n : ℕ)
    (M : Type*) [TopologicalSpace M] [T2Space M] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) M]
    [IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ M] [CompactSpace M] [ConnectedSpace M]
    (L : Type*) [TopologicalSpace L] [T2Space L] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) L]
    [IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ L] [CompactSpace L] [ConnectedSpace L]
    (ι : L → CotangentBundle (𝓡 n) M) (hι : IsExactLagrangianEmbedding ι) :
    HamiltonianIsotopic (𝓡 n) M (zeroSection (𝓡 n) M) (Set.range ι) := by
  sorry

end NearbyLagrangianConjecture

manifold of dimension $n$. Then every closed exact Lagrangian submanifold $L \subseteq T^*M$ is

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Nearby Lagrangian conjecture

The nearby Lagrangian conjecture (often attributed to Arnold) states that any closed exact
Lagrangian submanifold of the cotangent bundle $T^*M$ of a closed manifold $M$ is Hamiltonian
isotopic to the zero section.

Here $T^*M$ carries its canonical symplectic form $\omega = d\lambda$, where $\lambda$ is the
Liouville form $\lambda_{(x, p)}(v) = p(d\pi(v))$ and $\pi : T^*M \to M$ is the projection.
A Lagrangian submanifold $L \subseteq T^*M$ is *exact* if the restriction of $\lambda$ to $L$ is an
exact $1$-form, i.e. $\lambda|_L = df$ for a smooth function $f : L \to \mathbb{R}$.
Two Lagrangian submanifolds are *Hamiltonian isotopic* if one is the image of the other under the
time-one map of the flow of a (compactly supported) time-dependent Hamiltonian on $T^*M$.

Mathlib has neither cotangent bundles, nor the canonical symplectic form, nor Hamiltonian
isotopies, so these are defined in this file. Cotangent bundles are built from Mathlib's tangent
bundle and its bundle of continuous linear maps; the exterior derivative of a $1$-form on a
manifold is computed in a chart.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Nearby Lagrangian conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nearby_Lagrangian_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Ab12] M. Abouzaid, *Nearby Lagrangians with vanishing Maslov class are homotopy equivalent*,
  Invent. Math. 189 (2012), 251–313. https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.0358
-/

open scoped Manifold ContDiff
open Bundle

namespace NearbyLagrangianConjecture

section OneForm

variable {E H N : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [TopologicalSpace H]
  {I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H} [TopologicalSpace N] [ChartedSpace H N]

/-- The exterior derivative $d\theta$ of a $1$-form `θ` on a manifold `N` at the point `z`,
evaluated on the tangent vectors `a` and `b`.

A $1$-form is represented as a family `θ z : TangentSpace I z →L[ℝ] ℝ`, where (as everywhere in
Mathlib) tangent vectors at `z` are expressed in the coordinates of the preferred chart
`extChartAt I z`. The local representative of `θ` in this chart is
`θ' y = θ (ψ y) ∘ Dψ(y)` where `ψ = (extChartAt I z).symm`, and, with `y₀ = extChartAt I z z`,
$$d\theta_z(a, b) = (D\theta')(y_0)(a)(b) - (D\theta')(y_0)(b)(a),$$
which is the usual formula $d\theta(a, b) = \partial_a \theta(b) - \partial_b \theta(a)$
in local coordinates (cf. `extDeriv_apply` for forms on a normed space).
For a manifold without boundary and a differentiable `θ`, this is the exterior derivative of `θ`
at `z`. -/
noncomputable def oneFormExtDeriv (θ : (z : N) → TangentSpace I z →L[ℝ] ℝ) (z : N)
    (a b : TangentSpace I z) : ℝ :=
  let θ' : E → E →L[ℝ] ℝ := fun y ↦
    (θ ((extChartAt I z).symm y)).comp (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) I (extChartAt I z).symm y)
  fderiv ℝ θ' (extChartAt I z z) a b - fderiv ℝ θ' (extChartAt I z z) b a

/-- The exterior derivative of a $1$-form is antisymmetric. -/
@[category API, AMS 53 58]
theorem oneFormExtDeriv_swap (θ : (z : N) → TangentSpace I z →L[ℝ] ℝ) (z : N)
    (a b : TangentSpace I z) : oneFormExtDeriv θ z a b = -oneFormExtDeriv θ z b a := by
  simp [oneFormExtDeriv]

@[category API, AMS 53 58]
theorem oneFormExtDeriv_zero_left (θ : (z : N) → TangentSpace I z →L[ℝ] ℝ) (z : N)
    (b : TangentSpace I z) : oneFormExtDeriv θ z 0 b = 0 := by
  simp [oneFormExtDeriv]

/-- The exterior derivative of the $1$-form $x\,dy$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$ is $dx \wedge dy$, which
takes the value $1$ on the standard basis $(e_1, e_2)$. -/
@[category test, AMS 53 58]
theorem oneFormExtDeriv_xdy (z : ℝ × ℝ) :
    oneFormExtDeriv (I := 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ × ℝ)) (fun z : ℝ × ℝ ↦
      (z.1 • ContinuousLinearMap.snd ℝ ℝ ℝ : TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ × ℝ) z →L[ℝ] ℝ)) z (1, 0) (0, 1)
      = 1 := by
  have h : ((extChartAt 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ × ℝ) z).symm : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ × ℝ) = id := by
    rw [extChartAt_model_space_eq_id]; rfl
  simp only [oneFormExtDeriv]
  rw [h]
  simp only [mfderiv_id, id, extChartAt_model_space_eq_id, PartialEquiv.refl_coe]
  have : (fun y : ℝ × ℝ ↦ (y.1 • ContinuousLinearMap.snd ℝ ℝ ℝ).comp
      (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ × ℝ) y))) =
      fun y : ℝ × ℝ ↦
        (ContinuousLinearMap.fst ℝ ℝ ℝ).smulRight (ContinuousLinearMap.snd ℝ ℝ ℝ) y := by
    funext y
    ext v; rfl
  rw [this, ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv]
  simp

end OneForm

section CotangentBundle

variable (n : ℕ) (M : Type*) [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) M]

/-- The cotangent bundle $T^*M$ of a smooth manifold `M` modelled on $\mathbb{R}^n$: the total
space of the vector bundle whose fibre over `x : M` is the dual `TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x →L[ℝ] ℝ` of
the tangent space at `x`. The topology and smooth structure are those of Mathlib's bundle of
continuous linear maps from the tangent bundle to the trivial line bundle. A point `z : T^*M` is
a pair `⟨x, p⟩` of a base point `z.proj = x` and a covector `z.2 = p` at `x`. -/
abbrev CotangentBundle : Type _ :=
  TotalSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) →L[ℝ] ℝ)
    (fun x : M ↦ TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x →L[ℝ] Bundle.Trivial M ℝ x)

/-- The model with corners (without boundary) for the cotangent bundle of a manifold modelled on
$\mathbb{R}^n$: the product of `𝓡 n` with the model for the fibre $(\mathbb{R}^n)^*$. -/
noncomputable abbrev cotangentModel :=
  (𝓡 n).prod 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) →L[ℝ] ℝ)

variable {n M} [IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ M]

/-- The Liouville (canonical) $1$-form $\lambda$ on $T^*M$: at the point $z = (x, p)$ it is
$\lambda_z(v) = p(d\pi_z(v))$, where $\pi : T^*M \to M$ is the bundle projection. In canonical
coordinates $(q, p)$ this is $\lambda = \sum_i p_i\,dq_i$. -/
noncomputable def liouvilleForm (z : CotangentBundle n M) :
    TangentSpace (cotangentModel n) z →L[ℝ] ℝ :=
  (z.2 : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) z.proj →L[ℝ] ℝ).comp
    (mfderiv (cotangentModel n) (𝓡 n) TotalSpace.proj z)

/-- The Liouville form vanishes at points of the zero section. -/
@[category API, AMS 53 57]
theorem liouvilleForm_zeroSection (x : M) :
    liouvilleForm (zeroSection _ _ x : CotangentBundle n M) = 0 := by
  simp [liouvilleForm]

/-- The canonical symplectic form $\omega = d\lambda$ on $T^*M$, evaluated at the point `z` on the
tangent vectors `a` and `b`. In canonical coordinates $(q, p)$ this is
$\omega = \sum_i dp_i \wedge dq_i$. (Some authors use the opposite sign convention
$\omega = -d\lambda$; this does not affect the notions of Lagrangian submanifold or Hamiltonian
isotopy below.) -/
noncomputable def canonicalSymplecticForm (z : CotangentBundle n M)
    (a b : TangentSpace (cotangentModel n) z) : ℝ :=
  oneFormExtDeriv liouvilleForm z a b

/-- A family `φ : ℝ → T^*M → T^*M` is a *Hamiltonian isotopy* of $T^*M$ if it is the flow of a
compactly supported time-dependent Hamiltonian: there is a smooth `H : ℝ → T^*M → ℝ`, with all
`H t` supported in a fixed compact set, such that `φ` is smooth, `φ 0 = id`, and for all `t` and
`z` the velocity $\partial_t \varphi_t(z)$ is the Hamiltonian vector field of $H_t$ at
$\varphi_t(z)$, i.e. $\omega(\partial_t \varphi_t(z), v) = dH_t(v)$ for all tangent vectors $v$
at $\varphi_t(z)$. (The sign convention for the Hamiltonian vector field is immaterial: replacing
`H` by `-H` interchanges the two conventions.) -/
def IsHamiltonianIsotopy (φ : ℝ → CotangentBundle n M → CotangentBundle n M) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : ℝ → CotangentBundle n M → ℝ,
    ContMDiff (𝓘(ℝ, ℝ).prod (cotangentModel n)) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ∞ (Function.uncurry H) ∧
    (∃ K : Set (CotangentBundle n M), IsCompact K ∧ ∀ t, Function.support (H t) ⊆ K) ∧
    ContMDiff (𝓘(ℝ, ℝ).prod (cotangentModel n)) (cotangentModel n) ∞ (Function.uncurry φ) ∧
    φ 0 = id ∧
    ∀ t z (v : TangentSpace (cotangentModel n) (φ t z)),
      canonicalSymplecticForm (φ t z)
          (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) (cotangentModel n) (fun s ↦ φ s z) t 1) v =
        mfderiv (cotangentModel n) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) (H t) (φ t z) v

/-- The constant family `id` is a Hamiltonian isotopy (generated by `H = 0`). -/
@[category test, AMS 53 57]
theorem isHamiltonianIsotopy_id :
    IsHamiltonianIsotopy (fun _ : ℝ ↦ (id : CotangentBundle n M → CotangentBundle n M)) := by
  refine ⟨fun _ _ ↦ 0, contMDiff_const, ⟨∅, isCompact_empty, fun t ↦ by simp⟩, contMDiff_snd,
    rfl, ?_⟩
  intro t z v
  simp [canonicalSymplecticForm, oneFormExtDeriv_zero_left]

end CotangentBundle

/-- **Nearby Lagrangian conjecture.** Let $M$ be a closed (compact Hausdorff, without boundary,
connected) smooth manifold of dimension $n$ and let $T^*M$ be its cotangent bundle with the
canonical symplectic form $\omega = d\lambda$. Let $L$ be a closed exact Lagrangian submanifold
of $T^*M$, i.e. `L` is a closed smooth $n$-manifold, `ι : L → T^*M` is a smooth embedding whose
image is isotropic ($\omega(d\iota(v), d\iota(w)) = 0$) and on which the Liouville form is exact
($\iota^*\lambda = df$ for a smooth $f : L \to \mathbb{R}$). Then $L$ (that is, the image of `ι`)
is Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section: there is a Hamiltonian isotopy `φ` of $T^*M$ whose
time-one map sends the zero section onto $L$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 53 57]
theorem nearby_lagrangian_conjecture {n : ℕ}
    (M : Type*) [TopologicalSpace M] [T2Space M] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) M]
    [IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ M] [CompactSpace M] [ConnectedSpace M]
    (L : Type*) [TopologicalSpace L] [T2Space L] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) L]
    [IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ L] [CompactSpace L] [ConnectedSpace L]
    (ι : L → CotangentBundle n M)
    (hι : Manifold.IsSmoothEmbedding (𝓡 n) (cotangentModel n) ∞ ι)
    (hLag : ∀ q v w, canonicalSymplecticForm (ι q)
      (mfderiv (𝓡 n) (cotangentModel n) ι q v) (mfderiv (𝓡 n) (cotangentModel n) ι q w) = 0)
    (hexact : ∃ f : L → ℝ, ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ∞ f ∧ ∀ q v,
      liouvilleForm (ι q) (mfderiv (𝓡 n) (cotangentModel n) ι q v) =
        mfderiv (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) f q v) :
    ∃ φ, IsHamiltonianIsotopy φ ∧
      φ 1 '' Set.range (zeroSection _ _ : M → CotangentBundle n M) = Set.range ι := by
  sorry

end NearbyLagrangianConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition is appropriate: the statement is one universally quantified claim. The notes correctly identify that closed = compact, boundaryless and connected (connectedness is genuinely needed for both M and L) and that all of cotangent bundle, Liouville form/symplectic form, exactness and Hamiltonian isotopy had to be defined; the file does so with the bespoke definitions listed.
modeling_decisions: 'Closed manifold' is modelled as compact, Hausdorff (`T2Space`), connected (`ConnectedSpace`), smooth (`IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞`) and boundaryless (the model `𝓡 n` has no boundary); connectedness of both M and L follows the decomposition notes and is needed (for disconnected M or L the statement is trivially false). Second countability follows from compactness. `T2Space L` is redundant (L embeds in the Hausdorff T*M) but harmless.

Submanifold: L is given as an abstract closed n-manifold with a smooth embedding `Manifold.IsSmoothEmbedding (𝓡 n) (cotangentModel n) ∞ ι`; the submanifold is `Set.range ι`. Mathlib has no embedded-submanifold predicate; `IsSmoothEmbedding` (immersion in chart normal form + topological embedding) is the closest primitive and is equivalent in finite dimensions. Its smoothness consequence is `proof_wanted` in Mathlib but mathematically true.

Lagrangian: dim L = n is encoded by modelling L on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)` (same n as M); isotropy is `ω(dι v, dι w) = 0`. The isotropy hypothesis is mathematically implied by exactness (ι*ω = d ι*λ = ddf = 0) but is kept explicit to match the statement literally.

Exactness: ∃ smooth f : L → ℝ with λ_{ι q}(dι_q v) = df_q(v) for all q, v (ι*λ = df). Requiring f to be C^∞ rather than merely differentiable does not change the class of L (a differentiable primitive of a smooth 1-form is smooth).

Canonical symplectic form: ω = dλ (some authors use -dλ); the sign is immaterial for isotropy and for Hamiltonian isotopies (replace H by -H). The exterior derivative is computed via the chart at the point (`oneFormExtDeriv`); this is correct on boundaryless manifolds for differentiable θ, and λ is smooth.
Hamiltonian vector field convention ω(X_H, ·) = dH (rather than -dH): immaterial, as H ↦ -H interchanges the conventions.

Hamiltonian isotopy is parametrised by all t ∈ ℝ (not just [0,1]), required to be jointly smooth, with φ 0 = id, and generated by a Hamiltonian H_t whose supports lie in one fixed compact set K (following the '(compactly supported)' in the notes; standard for the non-compact T*M). By uniqueness of ODE solutions φ is then the (complete) flow of X_{H_t}, so each φ t is a diffeomorphism. This is equivalent to the un-cut-off / [0,1]-parametrised versions for this conjecture: any Hamiltonian isotopy moving the zero section to the compact L can be cut off to a compactly supported one with the same effect on the zero section, and time can be reparametrised.

Conclusion is `φ 1 '' Set.range (zeroSection _ _) = Set.range ι`, i.e. the time-one map sends the zero section onto L. The problem is not phrased as a question, so plain `theorem ... := by sorry` without `answer(sorry)`.

The Hamiltonian's smoothness is stated on ℝ × T*M via `Function.uncurry H` with model `𝓘(ℝ, ℝ).prod (cotangentModel n)`; the velocity is `mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) (cotangentModel n) (fun s ↦ φ s z) t 1`, which is the genuine derivative since φ is required to be smooth.

The Lean topology/manifold structure on `CotangentBundle n M` requires `[IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ M]` (the tangent bundle topology needs at least C^1), which is why the instance argument precedes the definitions using it.
